body: I don't think we have easy access to this platform. Could you try to see where the crash is coming from? You could try adding some printf statements to see where it dies approximately.
How can I invoke / debug the sandbox? I don't see any kind of tests on `src/main/tools/BUILD` or files. Any easy way of running it on gdb?
there is a --sandbox_debug flag. Does that help?

You can manually run the sandbox runner like this (where /tmp/bazel contains a current pull from Bazel HEAD):

philwo@philwo:/tmp/bazel$ src/main/tools/
philwo@philwo:/tmp/bazel/src/main/tools$ gcc -std=gnu99 -o namespace-sandbox namespace-sandbox.c process-tools.c -lm
philwo@philwo:/tmp/bazel/src/main/tools$ mkdir /tmp/sandbox
philwo@philwo:/tmp/bazel/src/main/tools$ ./namespace-sandbox -S /tmp/sandbox -M /bin -M /lib -M /lib64 -D -- /bin/bash
src/main/tools/namespace-sandbox.c:587: sandbox root is /tmp/sandbox
src/main/tools/namespace-sandbox.c:589: working dir is / (default)
src/main/tools/namespace-sandbox.c:282: unshare succeeded after 1 tries
src/main/tools/namespace-sandbox.c:400: createdir: /home/philwo
src/main/tools/namespace-sandbox.c:400: createdir: /nonexistent
src/main/tools/namespace-sandbox.c:416: mount: /bin
src/main/tools/namespace-sandbox.c:416: mount: /lib
src/main/tools/namespace-sandbox.c:416: mount: /lib64
src/main/tools/namespace-sandbox.c:524: arg: /bin/bash
bash: cannot set terminal process group (-1): Inappropriate ioctl for device
bash: no job control in this shell
bash-4.3$ echo hello
hello
bash-4.3$ exit

Running with gdb:

```
gdb --args ./namespace-sandbox -S /tmp/sandbox -M /bin -M /lib -M /lib64 -D -- /bin/bash
```

I get the following backtrace:

```
0x0000000000402d1d in SetupDirectories (opt=0x7fffffffe250) at namespace-sandbox.c:482
482   char *homedir = getpwuid(getuid())->pw_dir;
Missing separate debuginfos, use: debuginfo-install glibc-2.17-106.el7_2.1.x86_64
(gdb) bt full
#0  0x0000000000402d1d in SetupDirectories (opt=0x7fffffffe250) at namespace-sandbox.c:482
        homedir_from_env = 0x7fffffffef00 "/root"
        homedir = 0x4058ff "/"
#1  0x0000000000403ad1 in main (argc=12, argv=0x7fffffffe3b8) at namespace-sandbox.c:704
        opt = {timeout_secs = 0, kill_delay_secs = 0, stdout_path = 0x0, stderr_path = 0x0, args = 0x7fffffffe410, sandbox_root = 0x608170 "/tmp/sandbox", 
          working_dir = 0x0, mount_sources = 0x608010, mount_targets = 0x608080, mount_map_sizes = 12, num_mounts = 3, create_dirs = 0x6080f0, num_create_dirs = 1, 
          fake_root = 0, create_netns = 0}
        uid = 0
        gid = 0
```

So, geteuid() is returning **65534**, but centos uses uid 99 as nobody and 65534 is undefined, so getpwuid returns `NULL` and we have a segfault. I've changed the uid for nobody just for testing, and I get pass this issue. Now it fails trying to create `/` directory, which makes perfect sense, as nobody has `/` as its home directory. Changing it to `/nonexistent` (or anything else) and I have the sandbox working. 

Changes needed in the code to work with centos:
- Query nobody uid and gid.
- Check if homedir is `/`and don't create a directory in the sandbox.
- Check if getpwuid is not NULL

Time permitting I can post a PR with those changes.
Thanks for investigating, @pedrokiefer! I completely agree with you, your proposed changes should be made. I can have a look tomorrow, but would also gladly review & merge a PR.

repository.name: bazel

issue.body: 69fa69983b26c1059c99c7709162fbe778fe690f moved the [call to SetupDirectories](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/master/src/main/tools/linux-sandbox.c#L798) to come after [user namespaces](http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/user_namespaces.7.html) are configured. On systems where `/etc/passwd` maps user `nobody` to uid 65534 this still works, but on systems like Centos 7 where `nobody` is mapped to uid 99, this causes the [getpwud check in SetupDirectories](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/master/src/main/tools/linux-sandbox.c#L562) to fail, breaking all uses of sandboxing.
